standard.title: Perform in informal settings
standard.description: perform improvised and/or devised drama in informal settings
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can share drama in informal settings, considering audience perspective and reflecting on the experience (Y1-2). They can use elements of drama in dramatic play and simple performance.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students perform improvised and/or devised drama in informal settings, demonstrating commitment to role and using voice, movement and language to sustain dramatic action.

nodes.label: Sustaining role through performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can sustain role throughout a performance — including when not actively driving the dramatic action.
nodes.minimum_width: Student remains 'in-role' (through posture, expression, or attention) during a performance, including during moments when other characters are the focus.
nodes.typical_width: Students demonstrate commitment to the reality/world of the drama; they stay 'in-role' throughout the performance even when not actively participating in the dramatic action; they use voice, movement and language to sustain role and relationships.
wider: Students rehearse specific moments where role-commitment is tested — e.g. reactions to another character's action — and discuss what staying in role communicates to the audience
Students experiment with how physical stillness and focused attention in an 'inactive' role moment contributes to the overall performance
nodes.hinge_reason: Role-commitment is the foundation of performed drama; students who break role disrupt both the fictional world and audience engagement, collapsing the performance context and undermining the communicative work of the whole group.

response_modes.reason: Role-commitment develops through repeated short practice; use quick 'freeze-frame' exercises where students must hold role while the teacher or peers observe, building the habit of sustained presence.

success_criteria: Student remains visibly in-role throughout a performance, including during moments of inactivity
Student's physical presence — posture, expression, attention — is consistent with the role

nodes.label: Using voice, movement and focus to shape performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can manipulate focus, tension, space and time in their performance to shape dramatic action for an audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Student makes at least two performance choices (one vocal, one physical) that contribute to the drama's meaning and communication.
nodes.typical_width: Students vary facial expressions and movements to create roles and situations; they manipulate focus, tension, space and time to shape dramatic action; they use voice and movement in combination to communicate character relationships and dramatic situation.
wider: Students explore how changing one performance variable (e.g. deliberately slowing movement to heighten tension) transforms audience experience
Students take on contrasting roles in different performances, exploring how different character types require different vocal and physical approaches

response_modes.reason: Performance integrates role-commitment, element knowledge, and communicative intent. Post-performance reflection ('Did the audience experience what you intended? What would you change?') closes the loop.
Performing in multiple informal contexts — for a partner, a class, at assembly — builds adaptability and deepens understanding of audience relationship.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of performance contexts, role types and dramatic forms available at Y3-4 is broad; students who perform across multiple contexts develop stronger command of performance variables and audience awareness.
success_criteria: Student makes at least two performance choices (vocal and physical) that contribute to dramatic meaning
Student demonstrates manipulation of at least one dramatic variable (tension, focus, pace, space) in the performance
Student can describe a performance choice they made and explain what it was communicating
